rule: Every value below was returned by a function in reference/. Nothing here is hand-computed. Regenerate rather than edit.

vectors.note: msg = 32 zero bytes under the A1 key. Cross-checked against the reference's own committed expect_sig.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: WOTS+ signature construction

vectors.note: msg = 32 x 0xff under the A4 key. Every base-w digit at an extreme, exercising the WOTSLEN2 = 3 checksum chain.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: checksum digits are appended after the WOTSLEN1 message digits

vectors.note: msg = SHA-256 of the empty string under the A4 key -- a structureless, realistic digest.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: the signed message is a 32-byte digest

vectors.note: msg with only the least significant bit of the last byte set. With B5, pins base-w digit extraction order.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: base_w() consumes the high nibble of each byte first

vectors.note: msg with only the high bit of the first byte set.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: base_w() consumes the high nibble of each byte first

vectors.note: recover from B1's signature; must equal the A1 public key, and adrs must land on words 5-7 = {66, 14, 1}.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3(a): the adrs terminal state is message-independent

vectors.note: recover from B2's signature; must equal A4's pk.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3(a): the adrs terminal state is message-independent

vectors.note: recover from B3's signature; must equal A4's pk.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3(a): the adrs terminal state is message-independent

vectors.note: B1's signature with bit 0 of byte 0 flipped. A verifier that always succeeds also passes every positive vector; this is the control for that.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: recovery is sensitive to the first signature byte

vectors.note: B1's signature with bit 0 of the final byte (2143) flipped. Catches a length error that ignores the signature's tail.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: all WOTS_SIG_LEN bytes participate in recovery

vectors.note: B1's correct signature against a message with one bit flipped. Distinguishes message binding from signature binding.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: recovery is message-bound

vectors.note: the same signature produced with adrs words 5-7 zeroed and with them pre-set to the terminal {66,14,1}. Records whether the starting value of those words affects the signature, so a wallet that stores a post-keygen adrs and one that stores a zeroed adrs can be compared rather than assumed equivalent.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3(a): adrs words 5-7 are overwritten before use, so only words 0-4 are signature-relevant
